candidates.title: Jaylen Brown Out Wednesday With Hamstring Strain
candidates.excerpt: Jaylen Brown is set to miss the Philadelphia 76ers' matchup against the Orlando Magic on Wednesday with a left hamstring strain. Brown will be re-evaluated before Saturday's game against the Bucks. Brown suffered the injury late in the fourth quarter of Monday's win over the Nets. Brown is averaging 22.6 points and 6.6 rebounds on the year.

candidates.title: Jaylen Brown to miss 76ers game Wednesday vs. Magic due to 'hamstring strain'
candidates.excerpt: The Philadelphia 76ers will take on the Orlando Magic on Wednesday night, but without star shooting guard Jaylen Brown. He is dealing with a hamstring strain and has already been ruled out for tomorrow night's game. Brown picked up the injury during Philadelphia's win over the Brooklyn Nets on Monday. The guard is in his first season with the 76ers after the infamous trade that sent him to Philadelphia from Boston. Brown has played in 14 games so far this season and is averaging 22.6 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 3.6 assists. The Philadelphia guard had a slow start with his new team, scoring 19 points in his team debut. The 76ers have tried to find the best fit among Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Brown, and free-agent signee LeBron James. It finally seemed to be clicking for Brown ahead of the injury. He logged back-to-back games with 31 points, his season high. The guard finished Monday night's win with a double-double: 31 points and 13 rebounds. He shot just 47.4% from the field, but he made 10 of 11 attempts from the charity stripe as Philadelphia beat Brooklyn 135-123. Without Brown in the lineup, the 76ers will likely give more minutes to Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker. Wednesday's game against Orlando will be Brown's second missed game this season. He also missed Philly's first game of a back-to-back against the New York Knicks. Brown was dealing with both a head and a hamstring injury coming out of Monday's win against Brooklyn. candidates.title: Jaylen Brown ruled OUT vs. Magic with hamstring strain
candidates.excerpt: An impressive performance for Jaylen Brown on Monday night ended in a late exit from the contest due to hamstring tightness, Nick Nurse confirmed to reporters postgame after the Sixers’ win over the Nets. Now, Brown has been ruled out for Philadelphia’s Wednesday game against the Orlando Magic, listed officially with a left hamstring strain. Monday night had been a great one for Brown up to his exit — minus bonking heads with Julius Randle early in the fourth and ending up with a forehead cut, from which he returned to the contest. Brown tied his season-high with 31 points and grabbed a season-high 13 rebounds in the Sixers’ victory. There was no clear moment on the broadcast of the game that showed when Brown may have suffered the injury. Jaylen Brown ties his season high with 31 points vs. Nets, posting a double-double with 13 rebounds all in 33 minutes. 31 PTS, 13 REB, 4 AST, 1 STL, 1 BLK. Excluding the two NBA seasons shortened by COVID, 63 games played is the fewest total for him since he entered the league. He’s gotten this season off to a great start with his new squad, averaging 22.6 points shooting 38.6% from long range with 6.6 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.3 steals per contest. candidates.title: Sixers rule Brown out with hamstring injury for Magic game
candidates.excerpt: Sixers rule Brown out with hamstring injury for Magic game originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Jaylen Brown will miss his second game as a Sixer on Wednesday night when the team meets the Magic in Orlando. The Sixers listed Brown as out with a left hamstring strain on their Tuesday evening injury report. Brown had a head-to-head collision with Julius Randle in the fourth quarter of the Sixers’ win Monday over the Nets. He returned after a few minutes of game action with a bandage on his forehead, but Brown exited again with 1:44 left and did not re-enter. Brown’s only other absence this season came in an Oct. 30 victory vs. the Knicks because of left knee patellar tendinopathy. He scored 31 points in both games of the Sixers’ latest back-to-back. For the season, the five-time All-Star wing has averaged 22.6 points, 6.6 rebounds and 3.6 assists. Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction), Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear) all remain out for the 12-3 Sixers. The 6-7 Magic’s sidelined players include Paolo Banchero (right high ankle sprain) and Jonathan Isaac (left knee injury management).

candidates.title: CJ McCollum (Calf) To Miss At Least Four Weeks
candidates.excerpt: After injuring his left leg in Sunday’s game in Milwaukee and subsequently undergoing a medical evaluation and imaging, Hawks guard CJ McCollum has been diagnosed with a strained left calf, the team announced today in a press release. According to the team, McCollum will be reevaluated in approximately four weeks, which means he’ll be sidelined until at least mid-December. An update will be provided around that four-week mark, the Hawks say. After signing a one-year, $21MM extension with Atlanta in June, McCollum opened the season as part of Atlanta’s starting five alongside fellow guards Dyson Daniels and Nickeil Alexander-Walker. However, he was displaced during the first week of November by rookie guard Kingston Flemings, who made five straight starts before sitting out on Sunday due to a lumbar strain. Although McCollum has transitioned into a reserve role as of late, he remains a key part of the Hawks’ rotation, having scored at least 20 points in each of his past three outings. In 14 total games (nine starts), the 35-year-old has averaged 14.5 points, 3.9 assists, and 3.1 rebounds in 26.4 minutes per night, with a shooting line of .433/.352/.882. Flemings practiced on Tuesday, per Lauren Williams of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution (Twitter link), which suggests he should be back in action soon. McCollum sustained the injury in Sunday’s win over the Milwaukee Bucks. Imaging has since revealed the calf strain. He’ll be re-evaluated in four weeks, per the Hawks. Through 14 games, McCollum is averaging 14.5 points, 3.9 assists, 3.1 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game while shooting 43.3% from the floor and 35.2% from 3. The Hawks enter Tuesday at 8-6, tied with the Miami Heat for the fourth-best record in the Eastern Conference. The injury is a blow for the Hawks as they lose a key playmaker and their veteran voice on the court. McCollum, 35, began the season as Atlanta’s starting point guard. But he gave way to rookie Kingston Flemings in the starting unit, recently telling the NBA on Prime that he approached head coach Quin Snyder about making the lineup change. “I didn’t like the way we were playing as a unit, as a starting unit,” McCollum said. “I think we were a little sluggish.
